---
title: "Week 2 Exercises - Files, Directories, and First Pipes"
---

Short, **ungraded** practice tasks - about 20-30 minutes. Companion reading: [Ch. 4](../book/chapters/04-unix-fundamentals.html), [Ch. 7](../book/chapters/07-files-pipes.html), and [Ch. 8](../book/chapters/08-tidy-data.html).

1.  Inside `~/projects/comptools`, build a project skeleton in one command: `mkdir -p data/raw data/processed scripts results figures`.
2.  Run `ls -F` and confirm the five directories are there (the `/` suffix marks directories).
3.  Create a `README.md` with `nano`: type one sentence describing the project, save (`Ctrl+O`, Enter), and exit (`Ctrl+X`). Print it with `cat`.
4.  Download the course dataset into `data/raw` (the command is on the L02 slides and in [Ch. 1](../book/chapters/01-introduction.html#sec-course-dataset)). If you already downloaded it, `cp` or `mv` it into `data/raw`.
5.  How many lines does `Stickle_RNAseq.tsv` have (`wc -l`)? Given 80 fish, why that number?
6.  Look at just the first three lines with `head -n 3`. Too wide to read? Try `cut -f1-4 data/raw/Stickle_RNAseq.tsv | head -n 3` to see only the first four columns.
7.  How big is the file (`ls -lh data/raw`)?
8.  Make a copy called `stickle_backup.tsv`, rename it to `stickle_backup_2026.tsv` with `mv`, then delete it with `rm -i` (answer `y` when asked).
9.  In a scratch directory, create `file_1.txt`, `file_2.txt`, and `file_3.txt` with one `touch` command, then list them with the wildcard `file_?.txt`.
10. Save a directory listing to a file with redirection: `ls -lh data/raw > results/data_inventory.txt`, then `cat` it.
